I need a regex to match any digit in this string:
```
courses/163/content_migrations
```

Use:

```regex
\d
```

It matches each digit individually: `1`, `6`, and `3`.

For one or more consecutive digits, use `\d+`.

is this a good one-liner?

Yes, this is a good concise one-liner:

```js
/^\/courses\/\d+\/content_migrations\/?$/.test(location.pathname) && console.log("you are here.");
```

It matches the exact route with or without a trailing slash. For readability, I’d keep the `if` version if this grows beyond a single action.

there's only 1 <input> on this page and it has a click handler that inserts a span at the bottom of the page (it pretends to be a select), I need an onClick or an event handler or a mutation observer that removes all these list items except value empty, canvas_cartridge_importer and course_copy_importer
can't we use modern css `li:has(span[value]:not([value="none"]))` etc?
no, I meant for the querySelectorAll.

Yes. Use `:has()` to select the `<li>` elements containing disallowed options:

```js
document
  .querySelectorAll(`
    ul[role="listbox"] > li[role="none"]:has(
      > span[role="option"][value]
        :not([value="empty"])
        :not([value="canvas_cartridge_importer"])
        :not([value="course_copy_importer"])
    )
  `)
  .forEach((item) => item.remove());
```

In your existing function:

```js
const removeUnwantedOptions = () => {
  document
    .querySelectorAll(`
      ul[role="listbox"] > li[role="none"]:has(
        > span[role="option"][value]
          :not([value="empty"])
          :not([value="canvas_cartridge_importer"])
          :not([value="course_copy_importer"])
      )
    `)
    .forEach((item) => item.remove());
};
```

This uses `:has()` for selection, while `.remove()` performs the actual DOM removal.
